reported_case.shape: Full CLIP labels (including a bullet and colon) precede separate native media cards; no Done keyword. Model/specification disclaimer and progress messages separate the groups.

validation.label_attribution: The old parser fails the reported label-before-media fixture. Both leading and trailing bare labels now resolve only when a one-to-one relationship is forced across maximum matchings of neighbouring label sections. Ambiguous groups, pending labels, user turns, foreign results and old baseline media are not assigned by scene order.
validation.validated_bindings: Successfully downloaded files retain their original scene binding when earlier labels disappear from the native DOM. Direct filename/title/attribute and ARIA label references are considered without exposing their contents in reports.
validation.native_leading_fixture: Five opaque uniquely encoded MP4 files, bullet headings before media, no Done words or UUID filenames, delayed labels and progress interleaving complete in one chat message. Read-only retrieval compares the exact five byte sequences and adds no new messages/generations.
validation.multi_file_import: One file picker selection accepts mixed TXT/SRT, sorts filenames naturally, parses each file independently, preserves original names and multiline TXT prompts, and supports editing each source. Invalid/read failures reject the selection atomically.
validation.import_capacity: A 70-prompt import extends a contiguous 10-account/six-lane workspace from 60 to 70 queued slots without changing the ten accounts or six-lane setting; added slots repeat the existing account pattern. Custom hidden/nonconsecutive selections are not expanded automatically. All 401 cues remain visible as an over-capacity error, with loading disabled instead of silent truncation.
validation.first_wave_budget: Preparation, reference processing, generation, download/decoding and library save share the first-wave deadline from Create. A virtual-clock test spends 60 seconds preparing, verifies only 140 seconds remain in the API request, and ends loading at 200 seconds with one request and the full prompt preserved.
validation.backend_budget: The remaining integer waitBudgetMs is validated and bounded by the server's 190-second cap, subtracting body-read time. A short-budget integration test verifies abort and released capacity without generation replay. Newly admitted queued waves receive their own active-job budget.
validation.performance: Label extraction avoids compacting large URL/base64 strings; parsed file groups are memoized between status renders. Existing six-transfer/decoder queue remains independent of remote generation concurrency.

preserved_user_modes.standard: One lane per account; ten accounts = ten lanes.
preserved_user_modes.expanded_example: Ten accounts × six lanes = sixty concurrent requested slots.

validation.packaged_executable: Standalone EXE startup, ten concurrent images, exact named exports, restart persistence, ten shared-chat videos with six concurrent tasks, read-only native recovery with no new generation/chat message, explicit serial fallback and account-session media recovery.
validation.preserved_features: Full ordinary TXT/SRT prompts and names, automatic numbering, selected accounts and overrides, proxy/IP, session persistence, cancellation, composer preflight/isolation, renderer recovery and 200-second waiting limits.
validation.limitation: Automated checks use a fixture service and no live Muse credits. The user's actual five files were not accessed in this session. The deadline bounds tool waiting, not Muse's remote rendering time; later queued work starts when capacity becomes available.
